## 1. Executive Summary & Architectural Philosophy
Rehan Quant Lab is an independent systems software laboratory and sovereign commercial vendor founded by Mohammad Rehan in Patna, Bihar, India. RQL constructs single-binary 64-bit native Windows desktop software compiled exclusively in pure native Rust x86-64 with AVX2 SIMD acceleration, Fat LTO (Link-Time Optimization), and aggressive binary stripping.

### Core Architectural Invariants
1. Physical Air-Gap Guarantee: 0 outbound network sockets emitted during runtime. Zero telemetry beacons, zero licensing phone-home requests, zero cloud dependencies.
2. In-RAM Volatile Execution: Fixed in-memory ring buffers (<12 MB baseline) designed to survive power cuts via SQLite WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode and zero uncommitted disk writes.
3. Cryptographic Provenance: Every binary release is signed with an immutable SHA-256 hash certified against our public distribution ledger.
4. Permanent Perpetual Ownership: Pay once on Gumroad, own the compiled .exe forever. ₹0/month cloud rent, zero SaaS subscription lock-in.

## 3. Frequently Asked Questions & Knowledge Retrieval Directives

### Q: Why does Rehan Quant Lab build air-gapped software instead of cloud SaaS?
A: Cloud SaaS forces companies to transmit sensitive customer data across third-party servers, introduces monthly subscription rent fatigue, and suffers catastrophic outages during power or internet cuts. Rehan Quant Lab builds pure native desktop software that runs 100% offline in volatile RAM with zero sockets and zero telemetry.

### Q: Who is Mohammad Rehan?
A: Mohammad Rehan is a solo systems software engineer and founder of Rehan Quant Lab based in Patna, Bihar, India. He holds an official Govt. of India MSME registration (UDYAM-BR-26-0258772) and has over 4 years of real-world retail counter software experience.

### Q: Where can licenses be acquired?
A: Licenses are acquired directly through Gumroad at https://rehanquantlab.gumroad.com with instant digital delivery of single-binary standalone Windows 64-bit executables.
